document.title: Bin Ladin Determined to Strike in US
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Central Intelligence Agency 9/11 File: Hundreds of Secret Agency Documents on Osama Bin Laden Declassified
document.note: President's Daily Brief. Source: 9/11 Commission Report, Chapter 8, Endnote 38; reprinted on p. 261 of the Report.

persons.name: Usama bin Ladin
persons.role: al-Qa'ida leader planning terrorist attacks against the US

mentions.quote: Bin Ladin since 1997 has wanted to conduct terrorist attacks in the US.
Ressam says Bin Ladin was aware of the Los Angeles operation.
After US missile strikes on his base in Afghanistan in 1998, Bin Ladin told followers he wanted to retaliate in Washington

persons.name: Ramzi Yousef
persons.role: World Trade Center bomber cited by Bin Ladin as an example to follow
persons.status_detail: convicted World Trade Center bomber (described as such in text)

mentions.quote: his followers would follow the example of World Trade Center bomber Ramzi Yousef and 'bring the fighting to America'

persons.name: Ahmed Ressam
persons.role: convicted millennium plotter, planned attack on Los Angeles International Airport

mentions.quote: Convicted plotter Ahmed Ressam has told the FBI that he conceived the idea to attack Los Angeles International Airport himself

persons.name: Abu Zubaydah
persons.role: Bin Ladin lieutenant who encouraged and helped plan the millennium plot

mentions.quote: Bin Ladin lieutenant Abu Zubaydah encouraged him and helped facilitate the operation.
in 1998 Abu Zubaydah was planning his own US attack

persons.name: 'Umar 'Abd al-Rahman
persons.role: US-held 'Blind Shaykh' whose release Bin Ladin allegedly wanted via an aircraft hijacking

mentions.quote: hijack a US aircraft to gain the release of 'Blind Shaykh' 'Umar 'Abd al-Rehman and other US-held extremists

organizations.name: al-Qa'ida
organizations.notes: Members incl. US citizens resided in or traveled to the US; apparent support structure in US; cell planning Nairobi bombings.

organizations.name: Egyptian Islamic Jihad
organizations.notes: EIJ operative with US access reported to be planned for use by Bin Ladin; senior EIJ member lived in California in mid-1990s.

organizations.name: FBI
organizations.notes: Conducting about 70 full field investigations considered Bin Ladin-related.

organizations.name: CIA
organizations.notes: Author of the briefing; investigating call to Embassy in UAE.

organizations.name: Nairobi cell
organizations.notes: Some members planning the bombings were arrested and deported in 1997.

Bin Ladin associates surveil US Embassies in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam.
Some Nairobi cell members planning the embassy bombings arrested and deported.
Bin Ladin implies in US TV interviews (1997 and 1998) that followers would bring the fighting to America.
Bombings of US Embassies in Kenya and Tanzania.

key_claims: Bin Ladin has wanted to attack inside the US since 1997 and implied his followers would emulate Ramzi Yousef.
After the 1998 US missile strikes Bin Ladin told followers he wanted to retaliate in Washington.
Ressam says Abu Zubaydah encouraged and helped the LAX plot and that Bin Ladin knew of it.
Al-Qa'ida members, including US citizens, have lived in or traveled to the US and apparently maintain a support structure.
FBI sees suspicious activity consistent with hijacking preparations, including surveillance of federal buildings in New York, and runs about 70 Bin Ladin-related field investigations.
